chatHistory.content: # AEO B-Roll Animation Brief **Canvas:** 3840 × 2160 · 25 fps · ~1910 frames (~76.4 s) **Background:** `background_blue.png` via `staticFile()`, full canvas **Safe zone:** 210 px from every edge → usable area 3420 × 1740 starting at (210, 210) **Font:** Inter · **Transitions:** fade, 17 frames · **Spring default:** damping 200 --- ## Part 1: Raw Description (Shot-by-Shot) --- ### PHASE 1 — Compare the Three Engines (0:00:00:00 → 0:00:17:08) **Beats covered:** 1–4 (frames 0–433) **What the viewer sees:** Three large vertical cards appear side by side — one for each AI engine: **Google AI Mode**, **Perplexity**, and **ChatGPT**. Each card has the engine name as a blue header, a skeleton-line "AI Answer" block, and a citations section below. The cards stagger in from the bottom (left → center → right, ~12-frame stagger). Once all three are up, their citation pills fade in simultaneously: | Engine | Citation 1 | Citation 2 | Citation 3 | |---|---|---|---| | Google AI Mode | competitor-blog.com (amber) | techcrunch.com (green) | — | | Perplexity | reddit.com (amber) | techcrunch.com (green) | docs.example.io (amber) | | ChatGPT | wikipedia.org (muted) | — | — | Color logic: - **Green** = domain appears in 2+ engines (authoritative, shared) - **Amber** = domain unique to one engine - **Muted** = generic/non-competitive source After the citations appear (staggered ~13 frames each), a pulsing red warning badge fades in on the ChatGPT card: **"⚠ NEITHER OF YOU CITED"** — red-tinted card, 1.5px red border, pulsing opacity (sin wave, 0.5–1.0 range). At the same time, a second amber warning appears on Google AI Mode's card: **"⚠ COMPETITOR CITED — YOU'RE NOT"**. A bottom-center legend fades in last: - 🟢 Cited across engines - 🟠 Cited in one engine - 🔴 Gap — your brand missing **Takeaway:** Same query, wildly different citations. The viewer immediately grasps that each engine has its own source preferences. --- ### PHASE 2 — Look at the Sources (0:00:18:00 → 0:00:36:13) **Beats covered:** 5–10 (frames 450–913) **What the viewer sees:** A full-width card with two distinct zones: a **left column** showing a ranked list of "authoritative domains" and a **right column** showing a gap-analysis panel for "Your Brand." **Left column — Authoritative Sources (≈55% of card width):** A vertical list of 5 domain rows, each a horizontal bar with the domain name on the left and a citation-frequency bar on the right. They stagger in top-to-bottom (~15-frame stagger): | Rank | Domain | Bar width | Color | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | techcrunch.com | 92% | green | | 2 | wired.com | 78% | green | | 3 | docs.example.io | 61% | blue | | 4 | competitor-blog.com | 54% | amber | | 5 | yourbrand.io | 8% | red | Bar heights: 52px, rounded ends. Bars fill from 0% to target width via `barProg` spring. A small label at right end shows the percentage. A subtle header above: **"DOMAINS CITED ACROSS ALL THREE ENGINES"** — muted, 24px, uppercase, 0.12em letter-spacing. **Right column — Gap Analysis (≈45% of card width):** Once the bars finish drawing, the right panel scales in (spring from 0.88 to 1, translateX from 60px). It's an accent-bordered card (blue border, blue-tinted fill) containing: - Header: **"YOUR BRAND"** in white, 32px, bold - A large red percentage: **"8%"** — 96px, weight 900, red - Below: muted text "citation share" - A divider line - Three analysis rows that fade in sequentially (~13-frame stagger): - ✗ Missing structured data — red icon + muted text - ✗ No FAQ schema — red icon + muted text - ✗ Thin content depth — red icon + muted text - Below the analysis rows, a green call-to-action pill fades in last: **"Analyze what top sources do differently →"** — green border, green text, green-tinted fill **Takeaway:** The viewer sees which domains are authoritative and where their own brand falls short, with specific reasons why. --- ### PHASE 3 — Track Changes Over Time (0:00:36:20 → 0:00:52:00) **Beats covered:** 11–15 (frames 920–1300) **What the viewer sees:** A large full-width chart card occupies most of the safe zone. The card fades in with the standard entrance (translateY 50px, scale 0.92). **Chart header:** **"AI CITATION VOLATILITY — 12-WEEK WINDOW"** — muted, 28px, uppercase. **The chart itself** is an SVG area with: - X-axis: Week 1 through Week 12, labels in muted text at the bottom - Y-axis: implied 0%–100% (no visible axis, just horizontal grid lines at 25% intervals, rgba white 0.05) - **Two lines drawn with progressive reveal** (path length interpolates from 0 to full over frames 940–1100): **Line 1 — "Stable citations" (blue, solid, strokeWidth 8):** A relatively flat line hovering around 70-80%, with small fluctuations. Represents domains that stay cited consistently. **Line 2 — "Volatile citations" (amber, dashed, strokeWidth 6):** A wildly fluctuating line that swings between 20% and 85%, with dramatic peaks and valleys. Represents how much citations actually change. Once both lines are drawn, **two annotation badges** fade in below the chart (~15-frame stagger): 1. Blue badge: solid blue line swatch + **"Stable sources: ~30% of citations"** 2. Amber badge: dashed amber line swatch + **"Volatile sources: 40–60% churn monthly"** After a beat, a **large statistic** fades in center-right of the chart area: - **"40–60%"** in amber, 120px, weight 900 - Below: **"of citations change month to month"** — muted, 30px Finally, at the bottom of the card, a green pill fades in: **"Scheduled runs → full picture"** — green accent card style, with a small calendar/clock icon SVG on the left. **Takeaway:** AI citations are not stable rankings. They churn dramatically, and you need ongoing monitoring. --- ### PHASE 4 — Regional Data (0:00:52:00 → 0:01:07:17) **Beats covered:** 16–20 (frames 1300–1692) **What the viewer sees:** A world map visualization fills the canvas. The SVG world map (`assets/other/world.svg`) loads at 0.4 opacity, inverted + hue-rotated for dark theme, with a radial gradient overlay (blue center glow, transparent edges). **Three map pins drop in sequentially** (~25-frame stagger, spring entrance with scale from 0 + translateY from -30px): | Pin | Position (%) | Delay (relative) | Country | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | x: 22%, y: 40% | +15 frames | United States | | 2 | x: 51%, y: 30% | +40 frames | Germany | | 3 | x: 80%, y: 38% | +65 frames | Japan | Each pin: 48px blue circle with 5px blue-tinted border, glowing box-shadow, 4px stem below. **After pins land, info cards appear above each pin** (~35 frames after respective pin, spring scale from 0.7 + translateY from 30px): Each card is a navy-filled panel (blue border, rounded 24px, padding 32px 44px, min-width 480px) containing: - Country name as header: blue, 30px, bold, uppercase - Skeleton lines for the "AI answer" (2 lines, varying widths) - Citation pills unique to each region: | Country | Citations | |---|---| | United States | nytimes.com (green), competitor-blog.com (amber) | | Germany | spiegel.de (green), heise.de (green) | | Japan | nikkei.com (green), ascii.jp (amber) | **Key visual point:** The citations are DIFFERENT for each country — reinforcing that the same query yields different AI answers per market. **Footer callout** fades in at the bottom (translateY from 30px): A wide accent card (blue border, blue-tinted fill, rounded 20px, padding 32px 96px): **"Same query · Different AI citations · Every market"** — blue, 44px, bold, centered. **Takeaway:** AI answers are localized. International campaigns need per-market monitoring. --- ### PHASE 5 — Closing Statement (0:01:08:05 → 0:01:14:19) **Beats covered:** 21–22 (frames 1705–1869) **What the viewer sees:** A centered, minimal closing screen. # Phase 3 Fix: Relocate "40–60%" Stat + Smooth Chart Animation

---

## Fix 1: Relocate the "40–60%" Statistic

### Problem
The "40–60%" large statistic is currently absolutely positioned inside the SVG chart area (upper-right), where it collides with the blue "stable" line and the amber "volatile" line. It overlaps chart data and is hard to read.

### Fix
Move the "40–60%" statistic OUT of the chart SVG area entirely. Place it in its own dedicated row BETWEEN the chart and the annotation badges.

**New layout order (top to bottom inside the card):**
1. Header: "AI CITATION VOLATILITY — 12-WEEK WINDOW"
2. SVG chart (lines + grid only, NO overlaid text)
3. X-axis labels (Wk 1 … Wk 12)
4. **NEW: Stat row** — a flex container, centered horizontally, alignItems center, marginTop 40px, marginBottom 32px, containing:
   - "40–60%" — amber (#FBBF24), 96px (reduced from 120px to fit the row cleanly), weight 900, lineHeight 1
   - A thin vertical divider: 3px wide, 60px tall, rgba(251,191,36,0.3), borderRadius 2, marginLeft 36px, marginRight 36px
   - "of citations change month to month" — muted (#9CA3AF), 32px, weight 600, maxWidth 400px, lineHeight 1.4
   - The entire row enters via spring delay 120 (same as before), translateY from 20px
5. Annotation badges (blue "Stable" + amber "Volatile") — same as current
6. Green "Scheduled runs" pill — same as current

**What to remove:** Delete the absolutely-positioned "40–60%" overlay that was inside/on top of the SVG chart area. It should no longer exist as an overlaid element.

---

## Fix 2: Smooth Chart Line Animation

### Problem
The chart lines currently animate in a choppy, point-by-point way — the path jumps from point to point in discrete steps as `drawProgress` advances, causing visible "ticks" rather than a smooth draw-on effect. This is because the current `pointsToPath()` approach only adds whole points when `drawProgress` crosses a threshold, creating staircase-like reveals.

### Fix
Replace the point-filtering approach with an **SVG stroke-dashoffset** technique for smooth progressive line drawing:

1. Define the FULL path for each line upfront (all points connected, complete path string). Use straight `M ... L ... L ...` segments.
2. Calculate the total path length. You can hardcode an approximate value or use a ref to measure it. For a chart this size, estimate ~3200 for the volatile line and ~3100 for the stable line (adjust if needed).
3. Set `strokeDasharray` to the total path length (e.g., `strokeDasharray={totalLength}`).
4. Animate `strokeDashoffset` from `totalLength` (fully hidden) down to `0` (fully visible) using `interpolate()`:

```jsx
const drawProgress = interpolate(frame, [20, 140], [0, 1], {
  extrapolateLeft: "clamp",
  extrapolateRight: "clamp",
});

const stableLength = 3100; // approximate total path length
const volatileLength = 3200;

// In the SVG:
<path
  d={fullStablePath}
  stroke={COLORS.blue}
  strokeWidth={8}
  fill="none"
  strokeLinecap="round"
  strokeLinejoin="round"
  strokeDasharray={stableLength}
  strokeDashoffset={stableLength * (1 - drawProgress)}
/>

<path
  d={fullVolatilePath}
  stroke={COLORS.amber}
  strokeWidth={6}
  fill="none"
  strokeLinecap="round"
  strokeLinejoin="round"
  strokeDasharray={`24 12`}
  strokeDashoffset={volatileLength * (1 - drawProgress)}
/>
```

**Note on the dashed (volatile) line:** Since it already uses `strokeDasharray="24 12"` for the visual dash pattern, you need a different approach. Wrap the dashed path in a `<clipPath>` or `<mask>` that reveals progressively using a rectangle whose width is animated:

```jsx
<defs>
  <clipPath id="reveal">
    <rect x={0} y={0} width={chartWidth * drawProgress} height={chartHeight} />
  </clipPath>
</defs>

{/* Stable line — use dashoffset technique */}
<path
  d={fullStablePath}
  stroke={COLORS.blue}
  strokeWidth={8}
  fill="none"
  strokeLinecap="round"
  strokeLinejoin="round"
  strokeDasharray={stableLength}
  strokeDashoffset={stableLength * (1 - drawProgress)}
/>

{/* Volatile line — use clip mask for smooth reveal with dash pattern */}
<g clipPath="url(#reveal)">
  <path
    d={fullVolatilePath}
    stroke={COLORS.amber}
    strokeWidth={6}
    fill="none"
    strokeLinecap="round"
    strokeLinejoin="round"
    strokeDasharray="24 12"
  />
</g>
```

This gives both lines a smooth, continuous draw-on from left to right rather than jumping point-by-point.

### What to remove
- Delete the `pointsToPath()` helper function that filters points based on progress.
- Remove the per-point visibility logic.

---

## Everything else in Phase 3 stays exactly the same — grid lines, x-axis labels, legend badges, green pill, all spring timings for non-chart elements.
